decisions.difference: A: Unable to stand alone  vs  B: Unable to stand
decisions.reason: The page says "Unable to stand without support", which is standing alone; "Unable to stand" would miss a patient who can stand only with support.

decisions.difference: A: Unable to stand alone  vs  B: Unable to stand
decisions.reason: Same as the check_for decision: "without support" maps to "alone".

decisions.difference: A: Excessively deep breathing  vs  B: Deep breathing
decisions.reason: The page asks whether the patient was breathing "very ... deeply", which is excessive deep breathing, not just deep breathing (the two concepts are siblings).

decisions.difference: A: Excessively deep breathing (and its (no …) exclusions in the two vertigo rules)  vs  B: Deep breathing
decisions.reason: Follows the check_for decision on "very quickly or deeply".
The flowchart question asks about breathing "immediately before or during the collapse" after "Ask about fainting/collapse attacks", so collapse is asked about.

decisions.difference: A: hyperventilation requires Collapse; vertigo rules use (or (no Collapse) (and (no Tachypnea) (no Excessively deep breathing)))  vs  B: no collapse condition; vertigo rules use (no Tachypnea) (no Deep breathing)
decisions.final_expr: (and Dizziness Collapse (or Tachypnea Excessively deep breathing)); No branch: (or (no Collapse) (and (no Tachypnea) (no Excessively deep breathing)))
decisions.reason: The question's words, "before or during the collapse", presuppose a collapse; but the page doesn't say what happens to a dizzy patient who has no collapse, so this is unsettled.

decisions.difference: A: (>= (onset sudden-onset Dizziness) (time_ago 1 hours)) in vestibular neuronitis  vs  B: no time condition
decisions.reason: "Lasting hours/days" is the page's only difference between vestibular neuronitis and positional vertigo ("lasting seconds"); onset at least 1 hour ago is the closest the language gets, but it's an approximation of how long an episode lasts.

decisions.difference: A: Dizziness in positional vertigo rule  vs  B: (none)
decisions.reason: The whole flowchart is for "the patient with dizziness", and every other rule is anchored on Dizziness.

decisions.difference: A: Check for causes of dizziness  vs  B: Check for causes of dizziness not needing urgent attention
decisions.reason: B follows the page's box header "Approach to the patient with dizziness not needing urgent attention".

decisions.difference: A: Diagnose … with dizziness  vs  B: Diagnose … in dizziness / Diagnose probable positional vertigo / vestibular neuronitis
decisions.reason: Descriptions must be unique across the book; A's "with dizziness" ties every rule to this page, while B's bare vertigo/neuronitis names could collide with the ear page.

notes: Both builds passed. Base is A, because it is more faithful to the flowchart's collapse wording and "lasting hours/days". From B, only the causes task description is taken. B's extra clinician question (exclude positional vertigo from vestibular neuronitis) and its SNOMED-gap notes are merged into remaining-questions. Unable to stand alone and Excessively deep breathing are not in VHA's vocabulary.tsv; their siblings Unable to stand and Deep breathing are, but they fit the page's words less well.
